items.title: Stuart Bergen Interview, 1970-07-18
items.q: I still have Bill Voorhees on piano. And my front line is Earl Christian, Emil Christian and myself.

ctx.x: And I've been able to put the band across. I've been having a good man in my band. I might tell you my last lineup that I had when we played since Monk Hazel died I went with Emil Oyssen on drums. This is my latest band. I've been using Bobby Coquille on bass fiddle and I still have Bill Voorhees on piano. And my front line is Earl Christian, Emil Christian and myself. And they know my routine, they know my endings, the breaks. In fact Earl comes over here about every once a month and we just play together.…
You know we left a lot of stuff out. We haven't really got started yet. Do you have enough energy to go on?

items.title: Stuart Bergen Interview, 1970-07-18
items.q: And then your piano player. Bill Voorhees, the old Maple Leaf Ragman. That's what we call him, the Maple Leaf Ragman. And we have a tape with this band here on the other side.

ctx.x: Yeah, I could see Charlie Hartman and Chris on the tune. That's right. Christian, Earl Christian. And then your piano player.
Bill Voorhees, the old Maple Leaf Ragman. That's what we call him, the Maple Leaf Ragman. And we have a tape with this band here on the other side.
Oh yeah, I love it. And there's the Optimist jazzes, yeah. Well we better shut the thing off before we talk all day and I mess up. I have to meet a friend. All right, Ricky.
